name: Floor Sweeper
posted_by: Anonymous — single dead drop, Harrow Shelf transit node
target: A shift supervisor at the Harrow Shelf processing plant identified only as 'Muntz'
objective: Kill Muntz. No staging, no recovery requirement. Simple termination.
location: Harrow Shelf industrial processing zone, specifically the transit corridor between the plant's second shift exit and the Harrow bunk-stack residential node
complications: The target identification is a nickname only — the freelancer must confirm the correct individual before acting, and 'Muntz' may be known to more than one person in the plant community
Harrow Shelf is Tier 1 — ACS doesn't maintain presence, but the community maintains its own informal watch networks; a stranger moving toward the plant exit corridor will be noticed
Φ12,000 is at the low end of C-tier — either the posting entity has very limited funds, or they expect this to be an easy job, or both. Low pay correlates with poorly scouted contracts.
description:
Dead drop, anonymous, cheap. Harrow Shelf is a processing-plant district — shift workers, bunk housing, subsistence wages. The contract is bare-minimum: no staging, no attribution requirements, no recovery clause. It reads like someone with limited resources and maximum anger posted it. A new freelancer needing any work at all would consider it.

Muntz is a supervisor at the Harrow processing plant who has been reporting workers to a labor retention contractor — an entity that operates debt-bonded labor pools and pays a finder's fee for workers who are 'voluntarily' leaving their bunk-housing assignments. The workers Muntz has flagged have gone missing. The dead drop posting was made collectively by a small group of plant workers who pooled their wages over two months to afford it. They are not wrong about what Muntz has done. The freelancer, if they take this, is being paid by people who can barely afford food to remove a man who has been selling their coworkers. The moral weight is dirty not because the target is clean, but because the situation — the retention contractors, the debt bonding, the desperation that produces both the problem and the contract — is a machine, and killing Muntz turns it a quarter-rotation at most.
story_hooks: One of the workers who pooled money for the posting reaches the freelancer through the Harrow informal network and asks to be present — not to help, not to witness, but because they lost someone to Muntz and need it to be real

The labor retention contractor that Muntz has been feeding tips to has its own fixer who monitors for exactly this kind of informal elimination contract — they may move to protect their asset, which means moving against whoever accepts the job
